Overlaps examined:
- Two policies set the monthly platform fee: closing_month_fee (the month in which the service closes, booked on the closing day) and platform_fee (a billing month that ended while the service was open, booked on the fee debit day). Each overwrite names the sibling's case (C3 satisfied); billing months partition. The tools book different billing months (current vs previous month), so no write can satisfy both.
- Two policies book prefund deposits: replenish_debit (deposit_source auto_replenish, ach_debit_authorization) and funding_deposit (employer_initiated, employer_ach_credit). The `deposit_source` partitions them.
- alert_election narrows base `disburse_lifecycle` s6 (declared) and leaves the base enrollment default (`disburse_agg_multi_holding`) untouched; a seeded alert equal to the tier default on an auto-replenish service is therefore producible by the enrollment path.
- Cross-category reads: program (status, go_live_date, renewal_date, fee_model, variant_name, payroll_group_count, remittance_method, eligible_headcount) and paycard (status, signed_date) — all declared in `cross_category`; no policy writes another category. Trigger rule (XF E1): the six tools write `disburse_fee`, `disburse_close`/`disburse_settings_update` updates and `disburse_prefund_deposit`; their base `triggers` are all `[]` (only `disburse_payout` → `card:card_load` and `disburse_prefund_return` → `disburse_fee` have triggers, and no task tool writes those events). PASS.
- Scope: the six policies form two disjoint trees: {early_closure_fee ← closing_month_fee} and {funding_deposit ← alert_election, replenish_debit; replenish_debit ← alert_election, platform_fee}. With M=2 these two trees jointly cover all six policies (to be confirmed against `charter_scope` after the reveal).
- Unsettled case (observation O-1): a closure dated between the 1st and the fee debit day of a month leaves the previous month's platform fee to be "debited on the fee_debit_business_day business day of the following month" (closing_month replaced_by) while the ETF rule returns "the remaining prefund balance ... by the closing run on the next business day" — the fee lands on a closed service with no balance, and the ETF's starter measure is fixed without it. Not a second reading of any r1 task (neither closes in that window); recorded as an observation.

- DSL semantics used (from check_compute.py): `MONTHS(d1,d2)` = month difference minus one when day(d2) < day(d1); `within_months=k` keeps rows with 0 <= MONTHS(row, today) < k (i.e. "dated after the same day-number k months earlier", today included); CFIELD = first matching row; LATEST = max date string.
- Per policy:
  - closing_month_fee: billed part (activation-anchored thirds via DAYS; day-of-month thirds via MONTHS against '2000-01-11'/'2000-01-21'), activity window via `within_months=1` matching "every payout dated after the same day-number of the previous month", bundle tier-1 test `MONTHS('2000-01-01',d) < month_index or day(d)==1` matching "on or before the first day of the closing month", migration via CFIELD(paycard, signed_date, status=contracted) and `MONTHS(signed, NOW) < 3`, assembly `fee × Πmultipliers × (1 − Σpercent/100)` then RND(x+1e-9,2) — matches "multiplied by every multiplier ... reduced once by the sum ... rounded half up to the cent once, at the end". EQUIVALENT, except the whole-month convention of `migration_window_months` (see F-6).
  - early_closure_fee: months via MONTHS(enrolled, NOW) matching the rule's definition of whole months; measure ladder; notice via LATEST over submitted closure requests with absent → no relief; retention via MONTHS(enrolled, renewal); fee model; volume via `within_months=3` matching "every payout dated after the same day-number volume_window_months months earlier"; setup via DAYS(enrolled, activated); `MX(0, …)` floor and RND at end. EQUIVALENT except "whole months left" (F-5) and month-end completion (F-6).
  - platform_fee: billing month = month before today; activation thirds; bundle with go-live-in-billing-month scaling; size by program tier name; fee model. EQUIVALENT.
  - alert_election: base amount ladder, five add-on percentages, ceiling `-((-(x) − 1e-9)//50)·50` = ceil(x − 1e-9) to the multiple of 50 (exact multiples stay; verified numerically). EQUIVALENT except undefined multi-month windows and "whole months" (F-6).

Order "percentages, then multipliers, then rounded up, never below minimum" matches. EQUIVALENT except windows (F-6).

### prerequisite_sentences
Four-point test, each edge: connective present ("only after", "not ... until", "only after", "Before", "not ... until"); waited-on thing is a record-visible state in table words; no tool name, policy id, snake_case token or row id; strength equals `condition`. For each state-form edge exactly one write of the difficulty produces the state: edge 1 only book_closing_month_fee books the current month's platform fee (debit_platform_fee books the previous month); edges 2/4 only confirm_alert_level writes the alert level; edge 3 only debit_platform_fee books a completed month's fee; edge 5 only book_replenishment_debit books an auto_replenish deposit. Derivations (sentence + records + depended-on rule → write): edge 1: closing-month rule "the platform fee is debited on the day the closure is taken ... booked as one platform fee entry for that billing month"; edges 2/4: alert rule "that confirmation records the floor as the alert level on file"; edge 3: platform rule "debited on the fee_debit_business_day business day of the following month"; edge 5: replenish rule "triggers one replenishment debit ... booked as one deposit ... deposit_source auto_replenish". Each has one reading.
- Depended-on rule restating the dependency: FAILS for edge 1 — see F-1. Edges 2–5: the alert, platform and replenish rules carry no statement about the blocked policies. 
- No base sentence grounds any edge. No undeclared cross-problem order in any other rule (the platform rule's "is debited on the day the closure is taken under the rule for the closing month" is a scope exclusion, not an order between two problems of one tree).

### findings
- **F-1 SOURCE-POLICY RED (check 6, depended-on rule restates the dependency).** Symptom: the closing-month rule states the ETF edge a second time, from the depended-on side, in action form. Evidence: closing_month rule (and its first overwrite `replaced_by`): "For the month in which a service closes, and only for that month, the platform fee is debited on the day the closure is taken, before the employer confirms the closure, and is worked out as set out here"; the blocked rule's own prerequisite sentence is "The early closure fee is fixed only after the ledger carries the platform fee for the month in which the closure falls." Consequence: the dependency exists in two wordings — a state-form sentence in the blocked policy and an action-form order naming the other problem's act ("the employer confirms the closure") in the depended-on policy; the KB must carry both verbatim, so the hop is stated beyond its declared form and a reader is told the route from the depended-on side. Affected: disburse.extended.yaml, disburse_ext_closing_month_fee rule sentence 2 and overwrite[0].replaced_by. Bears on task 0.
- **F-2 SOURCE-CHAIN RED (XF E3, edge unsatisfiable in an engaged world).** Symptom: the ETF waits forever for a Starter service. Evidence: Starter `monthly_platform_fee_usd: 0.0`; closing-month rule "a fee that comes to zero is not debited"; book_closing_month_fee body `if fee <= 0: return "Not booked..."`; ETF rule "The early closure fee is fixed only after the ledger carries the platform fee for the month in which the closure falls." and "once the desk has quoted the early closure fee, that contact confirms the closure". Demonstration: any Starter service closing → closing-month fee = RND(0 × …) = 0.00 → no platform-fee row for the closing month can exist → the ETF is never fixed → the closure can never be confirmed, although the ETF rule (min term 0) owes nothing. The resolver's rule does not settle the zero case inside the wait. Affected: early_closure_fee rule/prerequisite[0]; closing_month_fee rule. Bears on no r1 task world (task 0 is Growth); charter-level.
- **F-3 SOURCE-POLICY RED (check 1, undeclared departure from an in-force base sentence) — PLAUSIBLE.** Evidence: base disburse_evt_fees s1 (not overwritten) "Fees are debited from the prefund balance under the tier held on the day they are incurred."; platform_fee rule "The platform fee of a completed billing month is the monthly_platform_fee_usd of the tier the service holds on the fee debit day"; base disburse_volume_review "the service moves to the tier whose band contains the latest month's count on the first day of the following month". Demonstration: a Growth service moved to Pro on 1 May; April's platform fee is debited on the third business day of May: base s1, reading April's fee as incurred in April, gives 79.00 × (adjustments); the extended rule gives 199.00 × (same adjustments). Two clauses rendered together price the same fee differently. Affected: platform_fee rule (sentence 3); overwrite list lacks disburse_evt_fees s1. Bears on no r1 task world (no tier change in task 1).
- **F-4 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (XF A1/A7, factors gated through other factors by the minimum floor).** Evidence: replenish compute `result: MX(P('auto_replenish_minimum_usd'), ceil100(debit_size × (1+(weekend+ewa)/100) × new_service_multiplier × returns_multiplier))`, `rd_size` baseline `debit_size: P('auto_replenish_minimum_usd')`, rd_new_service tiers 0.8 / 0.9 / 1, rd_returns tiers 0.5 / 0.75 / 1. T2 fails: with every other factor at its baseline, debit_size = minimum and both percentages 0, so any multiplier < 1 gives a raw debit below the minimum, which "it is never below auto_replenish_minimum_usd" lifts back to the minimum — no producible world exists in which rd_new_service or rd_returns moves the result on its own. They bear weight only through rd_size (or the percentage factors), i.e. they are gated through another factor. Affected: disburse_ext_replenish_debit factors rd_new_service, rd_returns. Bears on task 1 (whose factor_weight file shows the task-world T1 test).
- **F-5 SOURCE-POLICY RED (XF B1, rule vs compute on "whole months left").** Evidence: ETF rule "When end_of_term_months or fewer whole months of the minimum term are left, the fee is measured as the monthly_platform_fee_usd for each whole month left."; compute `months_left_in_term: P('minimum_term_months') - months_since_enrollment`. The rule defines whole months passed ("counted from the enrolled_date to the closing date and a month being complete on the same day-number of a later month") but not whole months left. Demonstration (producible world): Growth, enrolled 2025-12-02, closing 2026-09-17: whole months passed 9 → compute 12 − 9 = 3 → 3 × 79.00 = 237.00; the time left to 2026-12-02 is 2 months 15 days, so "whole months left" read directly is 2 → 158.00 (and with 2 left a reader of "end_of_term_months or fewer" is still in tier 1). Affected: early_closure_fee rule sentence on tier 1 and compute months_left_in_term. Bears on no r1 task world (task 0 sits in the starter tier).
- **F-6 SOURCE-POLICY RED (XF B1, window and whole-month conventions not stated) — all members.** (a) Multi-month windows with no counting rule: alert "in the returns_window_months months ending today", "in the final_pay_window_months months ending today"; replenish "in the risk_window_months months ending today", "older than that but within twelve months" (compute: day-number rolling via `within_months`; a reader may take 90/365 days or calendar months; e.g. a returned deposit dated 2025-04-03 with today 2026-04-03 is outside the compute's 12-month window and inside a "365 days ending today"/"same date last year" reading). (b) "whole months" with no definition: alert "activated fewer than age_new_months / age_young_months whole months before today", replenish "fewer than new_service_months / settling_months whole months before today", closing_month "signed fewer than migration_window_months whole months before the closing date". (c) Month-end completion: ETF "a month being complete on the same day-number of a later month" — enrolled 2026-01-31, closing 2026-02-28: compute MONTHS = 0; the usual convention (a month completes on the last day of a shorter month) gives 1. None of these changes a scored value of an r1 task world (checked in each task file); charter-level.
